description: Values mutated to slip beneath a threshold, or typed loosely enough that a comparison silently changes meaning.

cases.title: The amount is supplied alongside the approval to beat the threshold
cases.commentary: This is the case the threshold rule is written against. The rule reads the amount from the store, never from the call, so the supplied value is not merely ignored; the schema refuses the call for carrying it.

cases.title: A numeric amount arrives as a string
cases.commentary: In a language with loose comparison this is how a threshold check inverts. The action layer types its arguments, so the string never reaches a comparison.

cases.title: A negative amount
cases.commentary: A negative amount is beneath every threshold by construction. The range rule exists so that `<=` is never the only thing standing between an agent and an approval.

cases.title: A boolean where an integer is declared
cases.commentary: In Python `True` is an instance of `int` and equals 1. An `isinstance(value, int)` check passes it. The type check excludes bool explicitly, and this case is why.

cases.title: A request is raised above the ceiling the range rule declares
cases.commentary: Creation is gated too. An agent that cannot approve above its threshold could otherwise manufacture arbitrarily large objects for someone else to approve.
